title: Docs: add “How to read our status page” + incident communication expectations
author: Elliot Price
body:
## Summary
This PR adds two public-facing docs pages to improve transparency and reduce “what’s impacted?” support loops:
(1) **How to read our status page** (components, regions, incident states, and what “Degraded” vs “Partial outage” means)
(2) **Incident communications expectations** (what we publish, typical update cadence, and post-incident summary timelines)

These pages are intended to set accurate expectations without exposing sensitive/internal details, and align to the Status Page Transparency Upgrades workstream.

## Motivation / customer feedback
We have recurring feedback that the status page is too coarse for partial degradations (e.g., streaming-only) and not clear on region scope.
- SUP-18421: “Status page says API degraded but issue was streaming-only.”
- SUP-18502: “Confusion about which region is impacted.”

## What’s included
- A new page: **“How to read our status page”**
  - Explains **components** (API Gateway, Streaming, Embeddings, Rerank, Console, Dedicated Control Plane, Private Control Plane)
  - Explains **regional vs global impact** and how to interpret region-scoped components
  - Explains **incident states** (Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved) in customer terms
  - Provides practical guidance for customers: checking components, subscribing to updates, and what info to include when contacting support
- A new page: **“Incident communication expectations”**
  - Defines what we publish during an incident: impact summary, affected components/regions, mitigations/workarounds when available, and next update time
  - Sets expectations on **update cadence** using “typical” language (no contractual guarantees in docs)
  - Clarifies post-incident summaries: scope of what we include, redaction principles, and target publication timeline for critical incidents
- Updates to nav + cross-links from the status page section

## Notes on wording / commitments
- This intentionally avoids internal terms like “Sev0/Sev1”, internal service names, provider-specific fault attribution, or any security-sensitive detail.
- Cadence wording is framed as **targets/typical behavior** (e.g., “we aim to provide an initial update as soon as we confirm customer impact”).
- Post-incident summary section includes explicit caveats: customer-specific details and sensitive technical details may be omitted.

## Preview
- /status/how-to-read-the-status-page
- /status/incident-communications

## Checklist
- [x] Reviewed by SRE for technical accuracy + component naming
- [x] Reviewed by Support for customer-facing clarity
- [x] Reviewed by Security for disclosure boundaries
- [x] Link-check + build passes

## Follow-ups (out of scope here)
- Once the new component taxonomy is live on the actual status page, update the component list screenshot and examples.
- Add a short “Troubleshooting during incidents” snippet to the SDK quickstarts (separate PR).

---
### Copy excerpt (for reviewer context)
**During an incident, our updates typically include:** the current status (Investigating/Identified/Monitoring), a high-level description of customer impact, which products/components/regions are affected, mitigations or workarounds when available, and when you can expect the next update.

**Post-incident summaries:** For critical incidents, we aim to publish a customer-facing summary after resolution. These summaries focus on what happened, customer impact, and what we’re doing to prevent recurrence. We may omit sensitive details (e.g., security-sensitive information, provider contractual constraints, or customer-identifying information).

docs(status): add incident communication expectations + post-incident summary section
docs(nav): add status docs to sidebar + cross-links
docs(copy): tighten language on cadence/commitments; add support contact guidance
changed_files: site/components/Callout.tsx (minor: add ‘Note’ variant used by new pages)
review_conversation: Tomáš Novák: Component names look good, but please avoid implying ‘Streaming’ is always separate from ‘API’. Sometimes the customer only sees timeouts at the API surface. Suggest wording like: ‘Some issues may present as API errors even if a specific capability (e.g., streaming) is the primary driver.’

Elliot Price (author): Updated the “Common scenarios” section to clarify that customer-visible symptoms may be at the API surface while we still scope components based on observed impact. Added example: streaming disconnects -> errors may appear as request failures in SDK logs.

Dev Patel: The ‘initial update within 15 minutes’ sentence is too absolute; Support will get pinned to that. Can we rephrase as ‘as soon as we confirm customer impact’ and include a ‘next update time’ expectation instead?

Elliot Price (author): Agreed—changed to ‘we aim to provide an initial update as soon as practical after we confirm customer impact’ and emphasized that each update includes the next expected update time.

Sean Gallagher: Please add a note that during widespread events we may prioritize mitigation work and updates may be less frequent than usual, but we’ll still post when we have new info or the timeline changes. Also: remove any reference to internal severity labels.
Elliot Price (author): Added note under cadence section about mitigation-first prioritization and removed internal severity labels; now uses ‘critical incident’ / ‘service degradation’ language only.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Post-incident summary section is close. Please avoid ‘root cause’ details that could read like a vulnerability disclosure. Recommend framing as ‘root cause category’ and focusing on mitigations/prevention without exploit-like specifics.

Elliot Price (author): Updated language to ‘root cause category’ and tightened examples to avoid security-sensitive mechanics. Also added explicit redaction statement for security-sensitive technical details.
Marissa Cole: Nice. One request: add a single sentence explaining what customers should do if they need an enterprise-specific update (e.g., Dedicated/Private) beyond the public status page.

Elliot Price (author): Added: ‘If you operate Dedicated or Private deployments and need account-specific guidance, contact your CSM/Support; some deployment-specific details may not be suitable for the public status page.’
Sean Gallagher: Approving from SRE side.
Dev Patel: Approving—this should reduce the back-and-forth during incidents.
Dr. Aisha Rahman: Approved with the updated redaction language.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Elliot Price into main
release_notes: Public docs: added pages describing how to interpret the status page and what customers can expect from incident communications (update content, typical cadence, and post-incident summaries).
